persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
In a stream ahead of the jobs data he says he still finds the **S&P 500** cheap and is positive; indexes are flat but only tech is moving, and **Micron**'s earnings confirmed AI infrastructure demand. He attributes the rise in yields not to inflation but to US growth and the unwinding of the yen carry trade, and sees the 10-year falling back from 5.34% to 5.24% as a sign of relief.

He reads **Broadcom**'s search for $60B of financing for Anthropic as the reason for the pressure on the stock; once financing is settled it will be back on his radar. He says the US is trying to keep Hormuz open and that the real inflation pressure is in diesel, not crude. His own portfolio holds about 2.5% cash, gained about 8% in September, and he thinks October may not be very different.

items.title: Why I'm Positive on US Markets?
items.summary: Bora Özkent says he is positive on US markets ahead of the jobs data. Indexes are flat with weak participation; over the past month only tech has risen while banks and consumer discretionary fell sharply. The US 10-year hit 5.34% intraday, its highest since April 2002, then fell back to 5.24%; Bora attributes the rise not to inflation but to nominal growth and rising Japanese yields with the unwinding of the carry trade (10-year breakeven 2.36%, Fed target 2%). The ISM manufacturing index is 54.5, weekly jobless claims 197k, and the Q3 growth model estimate 3.7%. He expects roughly 90k jobs for September; he thinks a downward revision to August would show a seasonality problem and calm the market. He calls Micron's earnings proof of memory demand. Broadcom's search for $60B of financing for Anthropic may be weighing on the stock; if it is resolved the stock returns to his radar, and he finds the company cheap. Nike's earnings were bad again, with the stock down 8.5% in a day. The S&P 500's PEG ratio is at historic lows, so he finds the index cheap. His portfolio holds 2.5% cash, gained 8% in September, and he is positive for October too.

assets.note: He calls the earnings extraordinary: revenue up 379% year on year, 87% gross margin, 75% of 2027 capacity under contract; the stock sold off intraday but closed up about 3%.

persons.name: wallstengine
persons.digest:
He relays September payrolls (29k vs 90k expected; unemployment 4.2%), **Tesla**'s Q3 deliveries, eurozone September inflation at 3.8%, the highest since September 2023, and the France-Germany 10-year spread rising above 150bp, the highest since 2011. He writes that the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency diesel/crude stocks over four months.

He shares that **Broadcom** is assembling about $60B of financing for Anthropic, Morgan Stanley again made **Nvidia** its top semiconductor pick, the US will give **Vistra** a $4B nuclear loan and Amazon is exploring moving $8B of Nvidia GPUs into an SPV.

items.title: US September jobs report
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls +29k (est. +90k), unemployment 4.2% (est. 4.1%), average hourly earnings 3.0% y/y (est. 3.1%), participation 61.8%, private payrolls +46k (est. +81k).

items.title: Eurozone September inflation
items.summary: Eurozone September CPI rose 3.8% y/y (est. 3.7%, prior 3.2%), the highest since September 2023; core 2.5%, services inflation 3.2%.

items.title: France-Germany 10-year spread
items.summary: The spread of French over German 10-year yields rose above 150bp, the highest since late 2011, as worries about France's finances and political turmoil grow.

items.title: G7 emergency stock release
items.summary: Macron says G7 leaders agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency diesel and crude stocks over four months to ease pressure on fuel markets.

items.title: Broadcom $60B financing
items.summary: Broadcom is assembling roughly $60B of financing to help Anthropic and other AI customers fund chip and infrastructure purchases: $42B senior-secured debt and $18B junior debt led by Blackstone.

assets.note: Assembling about $60B of financing for Anthropic and other AI customers.

items.title: Morgan Stanley reinstates NVDA as top pick
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reinstated NVDA as its top semiconductor pick after a roadshow with Jensen Huang; power and data-center constraints favor NVIDIA's compute per GW and valuation is still "very undemanding".

assets.note: Relays Morgan Stanley's top pick call; power constraints favor NVIDIA's compute per GW.

items.title: Tesla Q3 numbers
items.summary: Tesla total deliveries 486,532 (est. 463,761), total production 464,391, Model 3/Y deliveries 478,237.

assets.note: Deliveries beat estimates.

items.title: $4B loan to Vistra
items.summary: He relays that the US will offer Vistra a $4B loan to boost nuclear power output.

assets.note: $4B US loan for nuclear output.

items.title: Amazon may move $8B of GPUs into an SPV
items.summary: Per the FT, Amazon is exploring shifting about $8B of NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs into an outside-investor-owned SPV and leasing the chips back, to reduce the upfront balance-sheet burden.

assets.note: Exploring moving $8B of GPUs into an SPV and leasing them back.

items.title: B. Riley downgrades ASTS
items.summary: B. Riley downgraded ASTS to Neutral from Buy and cut the price target to $65 from $85, saying risk/reward has swung back toward balance, citing stronger competitive alternatives, a delayed launch and rising constellation costs.

assets.note: B. Riley downgraded to Neutral; target cut to $65 from $85.
